title: The History of Age of Empires | From Ensemble Studios To Age of Empires IV | Gaming History
description: The history of Age of Empires: Ensemble Studios in 1997, Age of Kings, Age of Mythology, Microsoft, the HD and Definitive Editions and Age of Empires IV in 2021.
joke: In Age of Empires the strongest weapon is still telling your teammate to build more villagers.

sections.heading: Empires across history
sections.script: Welcome back to the channel. Today we are telling the history of Age of Empires, the real time strategy series where you guide a small village into a mighty civilisation. The first game launched in nineteen ninety seven, and the series is still active today, with remasters, new games and a huge community. We will go through the start at Ensemble Studios, the legendary Age of Kings, the mythology spin off, the third game, Microsoft's role, the return of the series with Definitive Editions, and the arrival of Age of Empires four in twenty twenty one. Our dates come from Wikipedia and from the official Xbox Wire retrospective written for the series' twentieth anniversary. Let us begin.

sections.heading: Ensemble Studios and a new idea
sections.script: The first Age of Empires was the first major game from Ensemble Studios, a small development team. The Xbox retrospective describes the studio as small in nineteen ninety seven, when Tony Goodman and colleagues made the first game. The idea was simple but fresh: instead of fantasy armies or space fleets, players would lead real historical civilisations such as the Egyptians, Greeks and Babylonians. Wikipedia describes it as one of the first history based real time strategy games. You gather food, wood, stone and gold, build a town, advance through different ages, and finally battle your rivals. Each age brings better buildings and units, and that sense of progress gave the game a clear and satisfying shape.

sections.heading: The first game arrives
sections.script: Age of Empires was released on October fifteenth, nineteen ninety seven, according to Wikipedia, and the Xbox retrospective says it came out in North America in October and worldwide in February nineteen ninety eight. It sold more than three million copies in its first three years and was one of the ten biggest hits of nineteen ninety eight. For a game from a small team, that was a huge success. It showed that history could be a great setting for a strategy game and that players enjoyed building an economy as much as fighting. The foundation for the franchise was now in place, and Microsoft was already planning to build on it. Many players first met strategy games through this title, learning the basics of scouting, expanding and managing an economy while the clock kept ticking.

sections.heading: The Age of Kings
sections.script: Age of Empires two: The Age of Kings launched on September thirtieth, nineteen ninety nine, and moved the series into the Middle Ages. The Xbox retrospective says it sold over two million copies in three months and stayed in the top twenty sales charts for more than two and a half years. Its expansion, The Conquerors, followed in two thousand. Many fans consider it the best game in the series, with a wide range of civilisations such as the Franks, Britons and Mongols, and a balance between economy, scouting and fighting that kept matches exciting. More than two decades later, people still play it online, and it is one of the longest lasting strategy games ever released. The Definitive Edition later brought it to a new audience, which shows how well its design has held up over the years.

sections.heading: Microsoft and Age of Mythology
sections.script: In two thousand one, Microsoft bought Ensemble Studios while it was preparing the first Xbox. The studio kept making Age of Empires games, and in October two thousand two it released Age of Mythology. Wikipedia lists the release date as October thirtieth. Instead of a purely historical setting, this game let players command Greek, Egyptian and Norse myths, with gods, heroes and fantastic creatures such as the Minotaur. The Xbox retrospective says it sold more than one million copies in less than four months. It was a bold change for the series, and many fans still love its mix of mythical units and the familiar Age of Empires economy and building style.

sections.heading: Age of Empires three
sections.script: Age of Empires three arrived on October eighteenth, two thousand five. It moved the setting to the age of exploration and colonisation, with explorers, settlers and trading posts. Wikipedia describes the game as covering the period from fourteen twenty one to eighteen fifty. The Xbox retrospective reports that it sold over two million copies in two years. The game introduced the home city, a system in which players built up a separate base that sent supplies and reinforcements to the map. It looked beautiful for its time and brought a different pace of play from the earlier games. Even so, many players still point to Age of Kings as the high point, though the third game has its own devoted fans who enjoy its different style.

sections.heading: The end of Ensemble
sections.script: Ensemble Studios worked on another project after Age of Empires three, the console strategy game Halo Wars. Wikipedia says Microsoft announced in two thousand eight that it would close the studio after that game was finished, and other coverage notes that the studio closed in January two thousand nine, shortly before Halo Wars launched. That was a sad moment for fans. The Age of Empires brand stayed with Microsoft. The series became quiet for a few years, with no new main game for a while, but players never stopped playing the old games, and new ways to keep them alive were already being discussed in the community.

sections.heading: The HD revival
sections.script: In two thousand thirteen, the series came back to life on Steam with Age of Empires two HD Edition. According to Wikipedia, it arrived in April and bundled the original game with The Conquerors, with updated graphics. The Xbox retrospective says that the HD remake has sold more than five million copies. The earlier Age of Empires three HD release had also sold two point four million copies on Steam. These sales showed Microsoft that people still loved the classics and wanted to play them on modern computers, and that a rebuilt version of an old favourite could find a big audience again. The HD editions also brought a new generation into online matches, and they made a strong case for finally making a brand new entry in the series.

sections.heading: Definitive Editions and Age of Empires four
sections.script: In June two thousand nineteen, Microsoft created the studio World's Edge to oversee the franchise. Age of Empires: Definitive Edition was released on February twentieth, twenty eighteen. Age of Empires two: Definitive Edition followed on November fourteenth, twenty nineteen, with help from Forgotten Empires, and Age of Empires three: Definitive Edition came on October fifteenth, twenty twenty. Microsoft announced Age of Empires four at Gamescom in twenty seventeen, with Relic Entertainment as the developer, and it launched on October twenty eighth, twenty twenty one. The Xbox retrospective says the franchise passed one billion dollars in sales in its first twenty years, with nearly thirty million players.

sections.heading: Your favourite age
sections.script: That is the story of Age of Empires, from a small studio in nineteen ninety seven, to Age of Kings in nineteen ninety nine, Age of Mythology and the third game, the closing of Ensemble, and the long revival through remasters and Age of Empires four. The series teaches a little history, rewards clever planning, and still brings friends together for long online matches. After more than twenty years, it remains a model of how a strategy franchise can grow and renew itself. So tell us, which Age of Empires game is your favourite, and which civilisation do you always pick? Maybe it is the Mongols, the Franks or the Egyptians. Share it in the comments below. If you enjoyed this history, subscribe to the channel for more franchise stories.
